convertibility_reason: Uses external custom signal library (ACDC_PL_RSI.mqh) for trading logic which requires manual analysis and reimplementation. The signal class CDC_PL_RSI is not a standard MT5 indicator and its internal logic is not visible from this file.

other_exits: Signal closes when CDC_PL_RSI signal value crosses below Signal_ThresholdClose (20) for longs, or above negative Signal_ThresholdClose for shorts

custom_logic_notes: The core trading logic is encapsulated in the CDC_PL_RSI custom signal class from ACDC_PL_RSI.mqh. Entry/exit decisions are threshold-based: the signal object produces a weighted vote (0-100 scale), and trades open when vote exceeds ThresholdOpen (40) and close when vote drops below ThresholdClose (20). The exact RSI/MA crossover or level-based logic inside CDC_PL_RSI::LongCondition() and CDC_PL_RSI::ShortCondition() is not visible from this file. Expert_EveryTick=false means the EA evaluates on new bar close, not every tick. Pending orders have a 4-bar expiration if Signal_PriceLevel is non-zero.
python_conversion_notes: The CDC_PL_RSI signal class from ACDC_PL_RSI.mqh must be analyzed separately to extract the exact LongCondition/ShortCondition logic. The EA uses the standard MQL5 Expert framework (CExpert, CExpertSignal) which handles position management, order execution, and signal aggregation. In Python, the threshold-based signal system (open at 40+, close below 20) needs to be reimplemented after understanding the custom RSI+MA filter logic. No digit adjustment logic is visible. The EA trades on bar completion (EveryTick=false), so bar-based backtesting is sufficient.
